answer: A comet-observation cooperative on a knoll issues one task ticket per certified secure module each round. A fable about owning many machines is insufficient: enrollment needs a manufacturer certificate and a fresh attestation. The module derives a stable round pseudonym from its fused secret, so resetting software or adding aliases cannot obtain extra tickets. A farm needs more genuine modules or a broken attestation chain, imposing hardware or exploit costs. This assumes duplicate enrollments are rejected globally; stolen devices, corrupt manufacturers and hardware monopolies remain problems.
